action.definition: Genre identity organized substantially around physical action and conflict.

adventure.definition: Genre identity organized around journeys, exploration, and peril.

drama.definition: Genre identity organized around sustained human conflict and emotional development.

thriller.definition: Genre identity organized around suspense, danger, and escalating uncertainty.

horror.definition: Genre identity organized around fear, dread, or horror.

science_fiction.definition: Genre identity involving speculative science, technology, or societies.

fantasy.definition: Genre identity involving supernatural or magical premises.

romance.definition: Genre identity centered on a romantic relationship and its development.

mystery.definition: Genre identity centered on uncovering an unknown or solving a puzzle.

crime.definition: Genre identity centered on crime, criminals, or criminal investigation.

western.definition: Genre identity drawing on frontier-western conventions.

neo_western.definition: Western conventions adapted to a modern setting.

giallo.definition: Genre identity drawing on stylized Italian mystery-thriller and horror conventions.

kaiju.definition: Genre identity centered on giant monsters and their impact.

disaster.definition: Genre identity organized around a major catastrophe.

superhero.definition: Genre identity drawing on superhero narrative conventions; powers alone do not establish membership.

zombie.definition: Genre identity organized around zombies or zombie-like contagion.

slasher.definition: Horror genre identity organized around a killer stalking and attacking victims.

creature_feature.definition: Genre identity organized around encounters with threatening creatures.

neo_noir.definition: Modern use of noir conventions such as fatalism, moral ambiguity, and criminal intrigue.

space_western.definition: Combination of western conventions and a spacefaring setting.

sword_and_sorcery.definition: Fantasy adventure organized around personal peril, swordplay, and sorcery.

cozy_mystery.definition: Mystery conventions with a reassuring social setting and limited graphic menace.

romantic_comedy.definition: Romance and comedy jointly organize the work.

melodrama.definition: Genre mode built around heightened emotional conflict and expressive plotting.

musical.definition: Genre identity in which musical performance is integral to storytelling.

war.definition: Genre identity substantially organized around warfare.

historical_drama.definition: Dramatic genre identity grounded in a past historical setting.

biographical.definition: Genre identity organized around the life of a real person.

true_crime.definition: Factual treatment of actual crime; fictional crime is insufficient.

psychological_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around perception, manipulation, or mental conflict.

conspiracy_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around concealed coordination and institutional danger.

survival_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around immediate survival under sustained threat.

legal_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around legal conflict and proceedings.

police_procedural.definition: Crime conventions emphasizing investigative procedure and institutional police work.

gangster.definition: Crime conventions emphasizing organized criminal groups and their internal lives.

whodunit.definition: Mystery conventions organized around identifying who committed a crime.

puzzle_box.definition: Mystery conventions inviting reconstruction of deliberately concealed narrative rules or structure.

space_opera.definition: Science-fiction conventions emphasizing large-scale space adventure and heightened conflict.

epic_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions emphasizing expansive worlds, large stakes, and extended quests or conflicts.

urban_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions combined with a recognizably urban, usually modern social environment.

dark_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions combined with a threatening or macabre horror-inflected atmosphere.

underdog_rise.definition: An initially disadvantaged character gains standing or succeeds against stronger opposition.

revenge.definition: Retaliation for a perceived wrong drives an arc.

vigilantism.definition: Characters enforce their own justice outside formal authority.

rags_to_riches.definition: A character moves from poverty to substantial wealth.

fall_from_grace.definition: A character loses status, reputation, or moral standing.

redemption.definition: A character attempts to make amends or change after wrongdoing.

mistaken_identity.definition: A character is consequentially taken to be someone else.

memory_loss.definition: Consequential lost or inaccessible memories, missing periods of time, or inability to recall one's own actions. Includes such gaps without a clinical amnesia diagnosis; does not require permanent loss. Ordinary forgetfulness and information withheld only from the audience are insufficient.

body_swap.definition: Characters exchange bodies or consciousness across bodies.

fish_out_of_water.definition: An unfamiliar social or physical environment challenges a character.

secret_identity.definition: Concealing an identity or maintaining a double life drives the story.

road_trip.definition: An overland journey with encounters along the way structures the story.

tournament.definition: A sequence of competitive rounds structures an arc.

training.definition: Learning or practice builds abilities toward a later challenge.

race_against_time.definition: A consequential deadline structures the conflict.

single_night.definition: The main action is concentrated in one eventful night.

locked_room.definition: An apparently inaccessible crime scene creates the central puzzle.

conspiracy.definition: Hidden coordination among powerful actors drives the plot.

apocalypse_survival.definition: Surviving societal collapse or a world-ending event drives the plot.

haunted_house.definition: An inhabited or visited dwelling is the focal site of a haunting.

chosen_one.definition: A character is singled out for a special, consequential role.

prophecy.definition: Predictions of destiny shape choices and events.

macguffin_quest.definition: Pursuit of an object whose plot function exceeds its intrinsic characterization.

final_survivor.definition: A surviving focal character confronts a threat after others are eliminated.

apparent_death.definition: A character appears to die but is later revealed to be alive.

mentor_death.definition: A mentor dies and the death matters to the mentee's arc.

doppelganger.definition: A double or lookalike produces meaningful events, identity confusion, recurring humor, or conflict. Antagonism or conflict is not required. Incidental resemblance without a narrative use is insufficient.

hidden_antagonist_reveal.definition: A character's antagonistic role is concealed and later revealed.

marriage.definition: Marriage and its obligations or conflicts matter to the story.

enemies_to_lovers.definition: An antagonistic relationship develops into romance.

slow_burn_romance.definition: Romantic development unfolds gradually through delayed intimacy or commitment.

queer_romance.definition: An explicitly depicted LGBTQ romantic relationship matters to the story.

workplace_romance.definition: A romantic relationship between coworkers matters to the story.

age_gap_romance.definition: A substantial age difference is consequential to a romantic relationship.

male_friendship.definition: Friendship among men matters to the story.

female_friendship.definition: Friendship among women matters to the story.

student_teacher.definition: A formal educational student-teacher relationship matters to the story; no romantic implication.

female_protagonist.definition: A woman or girl occupies a protagonist role, independently of competence or characterization quality.

child_protagonist.definition: A child occupies a protagonist role.

teen_protagonist.definition: A teenager occupies a protagonist role.

older_adult_protagonist.definition: An older adult occupies a protagonist role.

child_agency.definition: Children make consequential choices that affect events.

female_character_agency.definition: Women or girls make consequential choices that affect events.

lgbtq_characters.definition: Explicitly established LGBTQ characters have narrative importance; do not infer from allegory or creator identity.

neurodivergent_characters.definition: Explicitly established neurodivergent characters have narrative importance; do not diagnose from behavior.

disabled_characters.definition: Explicitly established disabled characters have narrative importance.

immigrant_characters.definition: Explicitly established immigrant characters have narrative importance.

travel_to_future.definition: Travel to a later time matters to the world.

lore_dependence.definition: Importance of remembering mythology or lore to follow the work.

cosmic.definition: Consequences extending beyond planetary life to cosmic reality.

cyberpunk.definition: High technology combined with alienation, social stratification, or countercultural urban imagery.

steampunk.definition: Retro-industrial speculative imagery drawing on steam-age technology.

neon_palette.definition: Use of luminous, neon-like color accents.

restricted_palette.definition: Use of a narrow or monochromatic color range.

aerial_viewpoints.definition: Prominence of aerial views, independently of capture technology.

closeups.definition: Prominence of tight framing on faces or details.

practical_effects.definition: Prominence of physical on-set effects; do not infer exact production method from appearance alone.

digital_effects.definition: Prominence of digitally produced or altered imagery.

costume_emphasis.definition: Expressive prominence of clothing and costume design.

split_screen.definition: Prominence of simultaneous images in separate screen regions.

aspect_ratio_changes.definition: Expressive use of changes in frame proportions.

grain_texture.definition: Visible grain-like image texture, independently of capture medium.

distressed_texture.definition: Deliberate wear, damage, or degraded-image treatment.

gun_fu.definition: Highly stylized choreography combining firearms and close-quarters movement.

environmental_choreography.definition: Creative use of surroundings and objects in action.

audio_self_reference.definition: Sound that acknowledges or plays with the work's representational frame.

nonmusical_sound_dependence.definition: Importance of non-musical sound to emotional or narrative understanding.

diegetic_music.definition: Prominence of music audible within the story world.

preexisting_recordings.definition: Prominence of preexisting recorded songs or pieces placed in the soundtrack.

live_performance.definition: Prominence of scenes depicting musical performance.

orchestral.definition: Orchestral music in the audible soundtrack.

electronic.definition: Electronic music in the audible soundtrack.

classical.definition: Classical traditions in the audible soundtrack; can coexist with orchestral instrumentation.

hip_hop.definition: Hip-hop or rap in the audible soundtrack.

folk.definition: Folk traditions in the audible soundtrack; name specific traditions in cultural annotations.

twist_impact.definition: Extent to which the ending reframes prior understanding.

cliffhanger.definition: Extent to which the ending suspends an urgent unresolved event.

sequel_dependence.definition: Extent to which another installment is needed to resolve central conflicts.

cyclical_return.definition: Extent to which the ending returns to or repeats the initial situation.

episodic_independence.definition: Extent to which episodes provide independently understandable stories.

serialized_dependence.definition: Extent to which episodes rely on ongoing arcs and prior episodes.

anthology_independence.definition: Extent to which episodes or seasons form distinct stories with separate continuity.

episode_cliffhangers.definition: Strength of suspended outcomes at episode boundaries.

bottle_episode_pattern.definition: Prominence of episodes deliberately limited in location or cast.

cold_open_hooks.definition: Prominence of openings designed to generate curiosity before titles or setup.

formula_repetition.definition: Recurrence of substantially similar plot patterns across episodes.

conceptual_renewal.definition: Introduction of new situations, ideas, or narrative directions across episodes.

attention.definition: Sustained concentration needed to follow the work.

visual_dependence.definition: Importance of watching the image to understand events; distinct from spectacle.

auditory_dependence.definition: Importance of hearing sound to follow events; accessibility version may alter this.

franchise_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with other installments to understand this work.

genre_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with genre conventions to understand this work.

historical_knowledge.definition: Need for historical background not explained in the work.

cultural_knowledge.definition: Need for cultural background not explained in the work.

onscreen_reading.definition: Importance of reading text embedded in the image; subtitle demand is derived separately per viewer and offer.

background_viewing.definition: Ease of following the work with intermittent attention; not inferred from pace alone.

drop_in_viewing.definition: Ease of joining after the start without significant confusion.

standalone_viewing.definition: Ease of understanding this work without other franchise installments.

discussion.definition: Scope for discussion of ideas, characters, or interpretation after viewing.

theorizing.definition: Scope for speculation about concealed information or unresolved mysteries.

repeat_discovery.definition: Scope for discovering additional details or interpretations on another viewing; distinct from personal desire to rewatch.

direction.definition: Assessment of coherence and execution of the creative vision.

acting.definition: Assessment of performance execution, not the presence of live-action performers.

dialogue.definition: Assessment of dialogue writing as a component of writing.

characterization.definition: Assessment of nuance and development in character writing.

narrative_cohesion.definition: Assessment of causal, structural, and thematic coherence.

cinematography.definition: Assessment of visual storytelling and photographic execution.

editing.definition: Assessment of shot assembly, rhythm, and transitions.

original_score.definition: Assessment of original musical composition, when present.

sound_design.definition: Assessment of the execution of non-musical sound.

intensity.10: Exceptionally strong or pervasive in the defined scope.

centrality.0: No narrative importance. The content may be absent or present without a meaningful role; use content_presence separately where covered. Zero alone never certifies absence.
centrality.10: Defining focus; removing it fundamentally changes the work.

membership.0: Does not use the genre conventions.

prominence.8: Prominent across much of the scope.

quality.10: Exceptional execution. Absence is not a zero-quality score.

suitability.0: Very poor fit under the stated assumptions.
suitability.10: Exceptionally strong fit. Not a universal audience verdict.

scope_rule: Every assessment belongs to an explicit movie, whole-show, season, or episode scope with an as-of date and coverage statement.
coexistence: Dimensions are independent; opposing or related traits can coexist. Do not force their scores to sum to a fixed total.

content_presence_definitions.tropes.memory_loss: Lost or inaccessible memories or missing periods of a character's own experience occur, whether or not diagnosed as amnesia. Ordinary forgetfulness or withholding information only from the audience is insufficient.
content_presence_definitions.tropes.doppelganger: A double or lookalike is presented as such; incidental resemblance alone is insufficient. Conflict is not required.
content_presence_definitions.relationships.coercive_group_control: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.
content_presence_definitions.characters.clandestine_groups: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.
